motions.item_title: Approve a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming December 2025 as Utah PTA Cent…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming December 2025 as Utah PTA Centennial Celebration Month. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: December named Utah PTA Centennial month
motions.summary: The council proclaimed December 2025 as Utah PTA Centennial Celebration Month.
motions.impact: This is ceremonial — nothing changes for residents. It's a public nod to the PTA's 100th anniversary.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing Item 13.A. - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Section 5.40 (Employee Credit Card Policy) of the Eagle Mountain City Employee Policies and Procedures Manual; and, including language in Item 13.B - Contract for Mortgage Assistance Program Administration with Ultimate Home Lending, LLC to state that the contract will be brought back to the City Council if loan applications exceed 100. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent items approved, mortgage contract flagged
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulling the credit card policy out and requiring the mortgage assistance contract to return to council if applications exceed 100.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day. If the city's mortgage assistance program draws more than 100 loan applications, the contract with its administrator comes back to the council for another look.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Section 5.40 (Employee Credit Card Policy) of the Eagle Mountain City Employee Policies and Procedures Manual
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Section 5.40 (Employee Credit Card Policy) of the Eagle Mountain City Employee Policies and Procedures Manual, and directed Staff to bring the item to a future Work Session for further discussion. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Employee credit card policy put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's employee credit card policy and sent it back for more discussion in a work session.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is an internal rule about how city staff spend on city cards, and the council wants another look before voting.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezone for Spring Run Plaza with the addition that the rights-of-way containing Roads A and B are rezoned to Agriculture
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezone for Spring Run Plaza with the addition that the rights-of-way containing Roads A and B are rezoned to Agriculture. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve Spring Run Plaza plan and rezone
motions.summary: The council approved the master development plan and zoning change for Spring Run Plaza, with the land under Roads A and B zoned Agriculture.
motions.impact: This is the approval that lets Spring Run Plaza move forward, so neighbors can expect the project to proceed. The motion doesn't state its size, its uses, or a timeline.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 6 and Title 17 to Establish Standards for Alternative Animal Management Plans and Update Other Zoning Provisions with the following addition: • The non-transferable Notice of Intent (NOI) is tied to the applicant rather than the property; therefore, the Animal Management Plan automatically terminates upon sale of the property
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 6 and Title 17 to Establish Standards for Alternative Animal Management Plans and Update Other Zoning Provisions with the following addition: • The non-transferable Notice of Intent (NOI) is tied to the applicant rather than the property; therefore, the Animal Management Plan automatically terminates upon sale of the property. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for keeping animals on your property
motions.summary: The city set standards for alternative animal management plans and tied the permit to the applicant, so it ends automatically when the property is sold.
motions.impact: If you keep animals under one of these plans, the approval is yours, not your land's. It does not transfer to a buyer — when you sell, the new owner has to apply on their own.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain, Utah, Amending the General Plan for Moderate Income Housing
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain, Utah, Amending the General Plan for Moderate Income Housing. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Moderate income housing plan updated
motions.summary: The council amended the moderate income housing section of the city's General Plan, the long-range document that guides future housing decisions.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for you right away. The motion doesn't say which housing policies were changed, only that the long-range plan was amended.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Annexation Policy Declaration as Part of the General Plan with the following conditions: 1. That the plan include the “Statement Addressing Comments of Affected Entities” as drafted by the City Attorney with the amendment that the SITLA and Saratoga Springs verbiage be omitted for the following reasons: a. The alignment in Area 6 matches the previous alignment from the Eagle Mountain City 2009 Annexation Policy Plan, and b. The annexation policy plan may overlap the plans from another jurisdiction, which would allow a property owner to have the option of which municipality would be most beneficial for annexation. 2. That the Annexation Policy Plan show Area 1 extending to Utah Lake, as presented, and 3. That the Annexation Policy Map show dates of previous versions of the annexation map/year it was approved, and 4. That the Annexation Policy Map show crosshatching for old property vs. newly expanded property boundaries
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Annexation Policy Declaration as Part of the General Plan with the following conditions: 1. That the plan include the “Statement Addressing Comments of Affected Entities” as drafted by the City Attorney with the amendment that the SITLA and Saratoga Springs verbiage be omitted for the following reasons: a. The alignment in Area 6 matches the previous alignment from the Eagle Mountain City 2009 Annexation Policy Plan, and b. The annexation policy plan may overlap the plans from another jurisdiction, which would allow a property owner to have the option of which municipality would be most beneficial for annexation. 2. That the Annexation Policy Plan show Area 1 extending to Utah Lake, as presented, and 3. That the Annexation Policy Map show dates of previous versions of the annexation map/year it was approved, and 4. That the Annexation Policy Map show crosshatching for old property vs. newly expanded property boundaries. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Update the map of land the city could annex
motions.summary: The council updated its annexation policy plan, extending Area 1 to Utah Lake and requiring the map to mark old boundaries separately from newly expanded ones.
motions.impact: Nothing changes inside the city today. This matters to owners of unincorporated land on the edges — the council deliberately kept overlaps with neighboring cities so an owner can choose which city to join.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Chapter 3.45, "Recreation, Arts, and Park Tax", of the Eagle Mountain City Municipal Code
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Chapter 3.45, "Recreation, Arts, and Park Tax", of the Eagle Mountain City Municipal Code. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New recreation, arts, and parks tax created
motions.summary: The city wrote a new Recreation, Arts, and Park Tax into its municipal code, adding a chapter that establishes the tax.
motions.impact: This puts the tax on the books. The motion itself doesn't state a rate or a start date, so check the ordinance for what you would actually pay and when.
